edges.description: Plaque disruption creates the local substrate for platelet deposition, coagulation cascade activation, and thrombus growth.
Persistent coronary flow obstruction deprives posterior left ventricular myocardium of oxygen and substrate, causing ischemic cardiomyocyte injury and infarction.
Posterior-wall injury is reflected by posterior-lead ST elevation and by reciprocal anterior precordial ST depression on standard 12-lead ECG.
Ischemic posterior myocardium activates cardiac sympathetic afferents, producing the acute chest pain in which the subtle posterior ECG signs are evaluated.

Failure to recognize STEMI-negative occlusion MI patterns delays urgent catheterization and reperfusion despite similar PCI needs, so the unrecognized posterior injury pattern feeds back on the ischemic node by prolonging the occlusion and enlarging the infarct.
intermediate_mechanisms: STEMI-negative occlusion pattern not recognized on the standard 12-lead ECG

edges.description: The modifiable and metabolic risk-factor profile does not disrupt a plaque directly; it acts through coronary atherosclerotic plaque development and progression, building and destabilizing the atherosclerotic substrate whose rupture or erosion initiates the acute coronary syndrome underlying posterior infarction.
ST elevation recorded in leads V7-V9 is the direct electrical sampling of the posterior injury current, so it reads out the posterior injury pattern rather than being caused by it.

Anterior precordial ST depression is the reciprocal projection of the same posterior injury current onto leads that face away from the infarct, so it is an indirect readout of that pattern on the standard 12-lead ECG.

A dominant early-precordial R wave is the mirror-image counterpart of posterior Q-wave formation. The cited study raises the alternative that it reflects a His-Purkinje conduction disturbance, so the link is recorded as a correlate rather than a direct readout.
Circulating troponin rises only after cardiomyocyte membrane integrity is lost, so it measures the posterior ischemic cell-death step and separates true infarction from ECG mimics.

nodes.description: Posterior myocardial infarction is usually a regional presentation of myocardial infarction, so modifiable and metabolic atherosclerotic risk factors for type 1 myocardial infarction, including LDL cholesterol, smoking, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, hypertension, and familial hypercholesterolaemia, are relevant risk contexts.

evidence.reference_title: From Atherosclerotic Plaque to Myocardial Infarction-The Leading Cause of Coronary Artery Occlusion
evidence.snippet: Factors predisposing to its occurrence include, among others, high levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in the blood, cigarette smoking, chronic kidney disease (CKD), diabetes mellitus (DM), hypertension, and familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH).

nodes.description: Rupture or erosion of an atherosclerotic coronary plaque can initiate acute coronary syndrome by exposing thrombogenic plaque contents and damaged endothelium to circulating blood.

evidence.reference_title: Thrombosis, physical activity, and acute coronary syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Acute coronary syndromes (ACS) are common, life-threatening cardiac disorders that typically are triggered by rupture or erosion of an atherosclerotic plaque.

nodes.description: Posterior MI presents in the acute coronary syndrome context, and chest pain may be the clinical context in which subtle posterior ECG signs are evaluated.

evidence.reference_title: Symptoms Predictive of Acute Myocardial Infarction in the Troponin Era: Analysis From the TRAPID-AMI Study
evidence.snippet: Symptoms including pulling chest pain, supramammillary right location, and right arm/shoulder radiation were significantly more likely to occur in patients with larger AMIs.

nodes.description: After plaque disruption, platelet deposition and coagulation cascade activation form a platelet-fibrin thrombus. This node maps that directly evidenced formation event to the module's formed-thrombus output. Its coronary-occlusion component is represented through the direct edge to the local ischemic-injury node; the mapping does not separately assert conformance to the module's upstream context, platelet-amplifier, or thrombin-generation nodes. When the thrombus obstructs a posterior-wall supplying coronary artery, such as the circumflex or right coronary artery, it causes posterior myocardial ischemia or infarction.

evidence.reference_title: Thrombosis, physical activity, and acute coronary syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Platelet deposition and activation of the blood coagulation cascade in response to plaque disruption lead to the formation of a platelet-fibrin thrombus, which can grow rapidly, obstruct coronary blood flow, and cause myocardial ischemia and/or infarction.

evidence.reference_title: Occlusion of the infarct-related coronary artery presenting as acute coronary syndrome with and without ST-elevation: impact of inflammation and outcomes in a real-world prospective cohort
evidence.snippet: Hs-CRP, lymphocyte, and neutrophil counts were independent predictors of total IRA occlusion, suggesting a possible role of systemic inflammation in the detection of TCO irrespective of ECG presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated posterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction: the necessity of routine 15-lead electrocardiography: a case series
evidence.snippet: Coronary angiography revealed a total/critical occlusion of the proximal circumflex coronary artery in all three cases.

nodes.description: A tall or dominant R wave, especially with R/S ratio greater than 1 in early precordial leads, can be a mirror-image ECG sign of acute posterior wall myocardial infarction.

evidence.snippet: The significance of the tall R wave in lead V1 with an R/S ratio  1 in posterior myocardial infarction (PMI) was investigated in 28 patients during programmed electrical stimulation.

nodes.description: Elevated cardiac troponin supports myocardial injury in acute occlusion MI definitions and helps distinguish infarction from isolated ECG mimics.

evidence.reference_title: OMI/NOMI: Time for a New Classification of Acute Myocardial Infarction
evidence.snippet: OMI was defined as an acute culprit lesion with TIMI 0–2 flow, or an acute culprit lesion with TIMI 3 flow intervened upon and with highly elevated troponin (cTnI > 10.0 ng/mL, hs-cTnI > 5000 ng/L)

nodes.description: Posterior-wall injury may be underdetected on standard 12-lead ECG because the posterior wall is not directly sampled. Reciprocal anterior ST-segment depression, especially maximal in V1-V4, and direct posterior-lead ST elevation identify posterior or posterolateral occlusion MI patterns that may not satisfy classic STEMI criteria.

evidence.reference_title: OMI/NOMI: Time for a New Classification of Acute Myocardial Infarction
evidence.snippet: Forty percent of patients with acute coronary occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) do not present with STEMI criteria, which delays their treatment and increases morbidity and mortality.

nodes.description: Coronary occlusion reduces oxygen delivery to posterior left ventricular myocardium. This node specializes Thrombotic Vascular Occlusion and Ischemic Tissue Injury; it does not represent embolization and does not imply unsupported conformance to upstream module stages. Ischemia disrupts calcium handling and mitochondrial function in cardiomyocytes; reperfusion is essential for tissue salvage but can add ROS and ionic imbalance, with necrosis and apoptosis contributing to infarcted myocardium.

evidence.reference_title: Mitochondrial and mitochondrial-independent pathways of myocardial cell death during ischaemia and reperfusion injury
evidence.snippet: Acute myocardial infarction causes lethal injury to cardiomyocytes during both ischaemia and reperfusion (IR).

evidence.reference_title: Mitochondrial and mitochondrial-independent pathways of myocardial cell death during ischaemia and reperfusion injury
evidence.snippet: There is also evidence for significant myocardial death by other pathways such as apoptosis, although this has been challenged.

evidence.reference_title: Mitochondrial and mitochondrial-independent pathways of myocardial cell death during ischaemia and reperfusion injury
evidence.snippet: Necrosis is known to play a major role in myocardial IR injury.

evidence.reference_title: Mitochondrial and mitochondrial-independent pathways of myocardial cell death during ischaemia and reperfusion injury
evidence.snippet: Mitochondria play a central role in both of these pathways of cell death, as either a causal mechanism is the case of mitochondrial permeability transition leading to necrosis, or as part of the signalling pathway in mitochondrial cytochrome c release and apoptosis.

nodes.description: When posterior MI reflects acute coronary occlusion, timely primary PCI is the key reperfusion intervention. Posterior-lead ECG and OMI recognition are important because STEMI-negative occlusion patterns can otherwise experience delayed catheterization despite similar angiographic PCI needs.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated posterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction: the necessity of routine 15-lead electrocardiography: a case series
evidence.snippet: Routine and accurate interpretations of 15-lead electrocardiography (12-lead with additional V7–V9) resulted in a better sensitivity for isolated posterior myocardial infarction diagnoses, followed by a timely and opportune primary percutaneous coronary intervention.

evidence.reference_title: OMI/NOMI: Time for a New Classification of Acute Myocardial Infarction
evidence.snippet: STEMI(−)OMI patients had significant delays in catheterization, yet had angiographic findings, rates of PCI, and complications similar to STEMI(+)OMI.
